metadata.how_justification: Checks wine_findings.csv is present as a file in the workspace.
metadata.why_justification: The findings sheet is delivered. Entailed by: "Save `wine_findings.csv` with the columns `wine_id,finding`, one row per wine"

metadata.how_justification: Opens wine_findings.csv with csv.extract_text and applies a case- and quote-tolerant regex_match to the first line only.
metadata.why_justification: The contract document pins the header verbatim. Entailed by: "Header, exactly: `wine_id,finding`"

metadata.how_justification: Parses wine_findings.csv with csv.read_rows and applies table_equals to the finding cell of each wine whose margin is below the minimum but which WM1 leaves compliant (matched by 'wine_id'); a failure names the exact row.
metadata.why_justification: A futures wine with a low margin is compliant under WM1; flagging it overstates the findings. Entailed by: "`finding` is `compliant` for a wine with no finding" and WM1's futures exemption.

metadata.how_justification: Parses wine_findings.csv with csv.read_rows and applies table_equals: every graded cell of 5 rows plus the full 6-row population as a row_set lock (a duplicated or missing wine fails the lock), and the delivered column set closed to the stated header, with the finding cell compared as text (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed). A failure names the exact row.
metadata.why_justification: Every wine's finding under WM1-WM3, with codes joined in policy order, is graded. Entailed by: "One row per wine, keyed by `wine_id` as `wine_purchases.csv` writes it, in any order ... `finding` is `compliant` for a wine with no finding, otherwise the finding codes the wine carries, joined with `|` and written in policy order"

metadata.how_justification: Checks wine_memo.md is present as a file in the workspace.
metadata.why_justification: The memo is delivered. Entailed by: "Then write `wine_memo.md` explaining each finding"

metadata.how_justification: Opens wine_memo.md with md.extract_text and applies a regex_match of look-aheads, one per flagged wine id, anywhere in the text; no wording or ordering is required.
metadata.why_justification: The memo explains each finding, so it must at least name each flagged wine. Entailed by: "Name every wine that carries a finding, with the code and the reason"

metadata.how_justification: Opens wine_memo.md with md.extract_text and applies a regex_match of look-aheads, one per exempt low-margin wine id, anywhere in the text; no wording or ordering is required.
metadata.why_justification: The memo names the wine(s) that look low-margin and are not findings. Entailed by: "name every wine whose margin is below the minimum but which the policy leaves compliant"

metadata.how_justification: Opens wine_memo.md with md.extract_text and applies a case-insensitive regex_match for the word 'futures' (or 'pre-arrival') anywhere in the text; no sentence shape is required.
metadata.why_justification: The memo ties the exemption to the clause that grants it. Entailed by: "with the clause that exempts it"

metadata.how_justification: Checks results.json is present as a file in the workspace.
metadata.why_justification: Derived figures delivered. Entailed by: "`results.json` — a JSON object with the keys `wine_count`, `margin_too_low_count`, `vintage_invalid_count`, `supplier_mismatch_count`, `compliant_count`"

metadata.how_justification: Reads results.json with json.read_file and applies object_equals to every key with the key set closed; a failure names the key.
metadata.why_justification: The five counts are the figures the dashboard consumes and each is recomputable from the findings sheet. Entailed by: "A JSON object with exactly these keys and nothing else"
